attributes.provenance: work_claim.offsetcast-investigation.20260831.v1. The harness itself surfaced two tool bugs that were fixed before these numbers were taken: file-local structs whose fields carry leading /* 0xNN */ markers parsed as zero-field structs, and an early candidate-scoring rule that named psfx.c's damage row from include/game/psys.h on offset agreement alone (now requires exact record-size match plus zero width conflicts, or the draft stays unkNN).

detail: Blind ground-truth test of tools/gdl/structdraft.py: run it against the PRE-conversion revision of a TU (which contains none of the recovered structs), then score the drafted offsets against the structs a human later hand-recovered in the post-conversion file. critter.c (checkout git:b7bdd105c~1, which has zero occurrences of CritterPackedType): the draft's observed offsets recover CritterDamageDef 20/20 named fields (100%), CritterFileHeader 15/18 (83%), CritterPackedType 42/51 (82%), CritterDescriptor 4/5 (80%), CritterHitNode 7/9 (78%), CritterColDescriptor 6/8 (75%); 226 of 477 observed offsets (47%) land exactly on a hand-recovered field boundary with matching width, the remainder being clusters whose ground truth is nested inside another record at a nonzero base or was left raw. screensaver.c (git:3cc9e36ef~1, zero occurrences of PanelConfigBlob): PanelPieceRow 6/8 named fields (75%), with the draft's x@0x04/y@0x08/width@0x1C/height@0x20 exactly matching the human's later layout. Reproduce: git show <rev>:<path> > old.c then `python tools/gdl/structdraft.py --file old.c --root . --json`. Coverage is bounded by what the TU's code actually reads -- a field no function touches cannot appear in a draft built from reads -- so coverage and precision are reported separately.
